hero.headline: Garage Door Roller Replacement in Wheaton
hero.subheadline: Worn rollers cause noise and damage. We replace them with quiet, durable parts. Get an upfront quote before we start.

intro: A garage door that grinds or shudders is a sign of component failure. Worn rollers strain your opener motor and can eventually force the door out of its tracks. We fix this by replacing the entire set of rollers, restoring smooth and quiet operation. Our trucks are stocked with high-cycle sealed-bearing nylon rollers that do not require lubrication, as well as heavy-duty 13-ball steel rollers for heavier doors. The job typically takes under an hour. A full replacement for a standard residential door costs between $120 and $220. As a family-owned business, we provide a firm, flat-rate price before any work begins. We are open 24 hours, Monday through Saturday, to handle your repair.
localContext: Wheaton’s mature oaks and maples are hard on garage doors. After a storm, it's common for twigs and seed pods to get crushed in the tracks, creating flat spots on old steel rollers. This is a frequent call for us in neighborhoods like the College Avenue area and Arrowhead, where homes from the 60s and 70s may have their original, unsealed metal rollers. The cycle of damp springs and humid summers accelerates rust on the roller stems. Even in newer Danada homes, builder-grade plastic rollers often crack under the strain of daily use and Chicago-area temperature swings. A bad roller can bend the track, leading to a more complex and expensive repair down the line.

problemSigns.detail: A metal-on-metal sound as the door moves. This indicates the roller bearings have failed.
The door shakes in its tracks instead of gliding smoothly. Rollers are likely misshapen or worn.
Look at the rollers as the door moves. If they aren't perfectly round, they need replacement.
Corrosion on the roller stem can cause it to bind in the hinge, stopping the door.

process.description: We inspect all rollers, hinges, and tracks for wear. You receive a flat-rate quote for the full replacement.
For safety, we unwind the torsion springs to take all tension off the door, cables, and bottom brackets.
We work panel by panel, removing the old parts and installing a complete new set of rollers.
We re-tension the springs, lubricate moving parts, then run a full balance and safety-reverse test.

whyUs: Family-owned and operated in the Chicago area.
Upfront, flat-rate quotes. The price we give is the price you pay.
Trucks are stocked with sealed nylon and steel rollers for most doors.
A full balance and safety test is performed after every job.

faqs.q: Why does my quote for a house in Danada differ from the base price?
faqs.a: Many newer homes in Danada have heavier, insulated doors. These require longer stems and higher-cycle rollers, which affects the flat-rate price.

faqs.q: Can you just replace the one bad roller on my door near downtown Wheaton?
faqs.a: We only replace rollers as a full set. When one fails, the others have the same amount of wear. Mismatched rollers cause uneven operation and can damage your tracks.

faqs.q: How soon can you get to my home in Arrowhead for a roller job?
faqs.a: We offer same-day service in Wheaton. Because roller replacement is not an emergency, we schedule it around urgent calls. We can typically complete the job in a single visit.

faqs.q: My tracks are full of debris from my oak tree. Is cleaning them included?
faqs.a: Yes. As part of any roller replacement in Wheaton, we clear and inspect the tracks. Obstructed tracks are a primary cause of roller failure in the area.

faqs.q: Is the $120-$220 price firm for parts and labor?
faqs.a: That range covers the complete job for most standard doors. The final flat-rate price depends on your door's size, weight, and the type of rollers you select. You approve the quote before we begin.
